title: My Heart, How Dreadful Hard It Is
description: My Heart, How Dreadful Hard It Is in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 98, headed “Hardness of heart complained of”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: My heart, how dread-ful hard it is! How hea-vy here it lies, Hea-vy and cold with-in my breast Just like a rock of ice!

lines: My heart, how dreadful hard it is!
How heavy here it lies,
Heavy and cold within my breast
Just like a rock of ice!
Sin like a raging tyrant sits
Upon this flinty throne,
And every grace lies buried deep
Beneath this heart of stone.
How seldom do I rise to God,
Or taste the joys above!
This mountain presses down my faith,
And chills my flaming love.
When smiling mercy courts my soul
With all its heavenly charms,
This stubborn, this relentless thing
Would thrust it from my arms.
Against the thunders of thy word
Rebellious I have stood,
My heart it shakes not at the wrath
And terrors of a God.
Dear Saviour, steep this rock of mine
In thine own crimson sea:
None but a bath of blood divine
Can melt the flint away.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
